modules.name: Introduction to Organic Compounds and Hydrocarbons

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
• Organic Compounds:
 Primarily composed of carbon and hydrogen atoms, with potential inclusion of nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur, and halogens.

• Hydrocarbons:
 Simplest organic compounds made solely of carbon and hydrogen.

blocks.title: Closed chain and Cyclic Compound
blocks.text:
• Homocyclic Compound

A molecule with a ring structure made up of only carbon atoms.

• Heterocyclic Compound

A cyclic compound that has atoms of at least two different elements as members of its ring(s).

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.question: Identify the type of hydrocarbon with the formula $C_4H_8$.

(A) 8

(B) 12

(D) 4

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.text:
• Assuming all carbon-containing compounds are organic, ignoring exceptions like carbonates (e.g., $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$) and oxides of carbon (e.g., $\mathrm{CO_2}$).
  • Failing to differentiate between structural formulas, condensed formulas, and skeletal structures.
  • Misclassifying aromatic compounds (e.g., benzene) as alkenes due to the presence of double bonds without considering delocalized π-electrons.

blocks.text:
• Placing atoms or bonds incorrectly results in structures that violate the valency rules of atoms (e.g., carbon with five bonds).
  • Forgetting to show lone pairs on heteroatoms or charges on atoms in ionic species.
  • Misrepresenting or misunderstanding the branching of substituents on the main chain.
  • Using wedges and dashes incorrectly to indicate stereochemistry, leading to wrong spatial configurations.

modules.name: Types of Carbon Atoms and Hybridization

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Types of Carbon Atoms:

  • Primary (1°): Carbon atom attached to one other carbon.
  • Secondary (2°): Carbon atom attached to two other carbons.
  • Tertiary (3°): Carbon atom attached to three other carbons.
  • Quaternary (4°): Carbon atom attached to four other carbons.
Hybridization:

  • Determines molecular geometry and bond angles.
  • Types include sp³, sp², and sp hybridization.

blocks.title: Formulas & Mathematical Relations
blocks.text:
• Hybridization Formula: Steric Number(SN)
$\text{SN} = \text{sigma bonds} + \text{lone pairs}$
  • sp³ Hybridization:
$\text{SN} = 4 \quad (\text{Tetrahedral, } 109.5^\circ)$
  • sp² Hybridization:
$\text{SN} = 3 \quad (\text{Trigonal Planar, } 120^\circ)$
  • sp Hybridization:
$\text{SN} = 2 \quad (\text{Linear, } 180^\circ)$

blocks.title: Memorization Techniques
blocks.text:
• Acronym: "Tetra, Tri, two" for remembering sp³, sp², sp.
  • NEET Strategy: Count sigma bonds and lone pairs around the carbon atom to determine hybridization.

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
• Mistaking pi bonds for sigma bonds.
  • Forgetting that lone pairs contribute to the steric number (SN).

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Functional Groups:

  • Specific groups of atoms are responsible for characteristic chemical reactions.
Examples include:

  • Alcohols: -OH
  • Carboxylic acids: -COOH
  • Amines: -NH₂
Homologous Series:

  • Compounds that share the same functional group and differ by a CH₂ unit.
  • They show similar chemical properties and a gradation in physical properties.

blocks.title: Formulas & Mathematical Relations
blocks.text: Homologous series and functional group

blocks.title: DATA
blocks.text:
Functional Group Priority:

  • Carboxylic acid > Sulphonic acid > Anhydride > Ester > Acid halide > Amide > Cyanide > Isocyanide > Aldehyde > Ketone > Alcohol >Thio alcohol > Amine.
Boiling Point Trend:

  • Boiling points increase with molecular weight in a homologous series.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.question:
The IUPAC name of the above compound is
(A) 2-Acetoxyethanoic acid
(B) 2-Methoxycarbonyletanoic acid
(C) 3-Methoxycarbonyletanoic acid
(D) 2-Methoxyformylacetic acid
blocks.answer:
Answer: (B)

Solution:

  • Recognize the functional group -COOH, which is indicative of carboxylic acids.
  • Name the compound as "acetic acid" or "ethanoic acid".

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text:
• Confusing the functional group with the parent hydrocarbon chain.
  • Forgetting the priority order for IUPAC naming.
  • Misapplying general formulas in cyclic compounds.
These notes provide a structured and thorough review of functional groups and homologous series, beneficial for NEET aspirants.

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
• IUPAC (International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry) nomenclature provides a systematic method for naming organic compounds, ensuring unique and universally accepted names.
  • Format for IUPAC name :    s-prefix  + p-prefix +  word root + p-suffix + s-suffix
  • Identify the longest carbon chain.
  • Prioritize principle  functional groups based on IUPAC rules.
  • Number the chain to give the lowest set of locants  to substituents and functional groups.
  • In complex names, primary and secondary prefixes are combined in the order:
  • Secondary Prefix (substituents)
  • Primary Prefix (general type of compound)
  • Root Name (number of carbons in the main chain)
  • Secondary Suffix (main functional group)
Example: 1-Bromo-2-methylcyclopropane

  • Secondary Prefixes: "Bromo-" and "Methyl-" (substituents).
  • Primary Prefix: "Cyclo-" (indicating a ring structure).
  • Root Name: "Propane" (3 carbons).
  • Full Name: 1-Bromo-2-methylcyclopropane.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.question: Name the compound with the molecular structure: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃.
blocks.prompt: Name the compound with the molecular structure: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃.

blocks.title: Common Mistakes
blocks.text: Note:   Always follow  Priority Order:  Functional Group > Multiple bond >Number of C-atom >Side substituent

blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
• Priority of functional groups in organic nomenclature determines the suffix or prefix and numbering of the carbon chain, as per IUPAC rules.
Naming of Alkyl Groups (Radicals) :

$\text{Alkane} \xrightarrow{-H} \text{Alkyl} \quad
$

$\text{Alkene} \xrightarrow{-H} \text{Alkenyl}$

$\text{Alkyne} \xrightarrow{-H} \text{Alkynyl}$

blocks.title: Formulas & Mathematical Relations
blocks.text:
Priority Order:
$\text{Carboxylic acids} > \text{Anhydrides} > \text{Esters} > \text{Acid halides} > \text{Amides} > \text{Nitriles} > \text{Aldehydes} > \text{Ketones} > \text{Alcohols} > \text{Amines} $

Numbering Rule Application:

  • The carbon chain is numbered to give the highest priority group the lowest possible number.

blocks.question: Assign the IUPAC name to a compound with the structure: CH₃COOCH₂CH₃.
blocks.prompt: Assign the IUPAC name to a compound with the structure: CH₃COOCH₂CH₃.
